page.layout: Top: two coin medallions side by side, each with its legend around the rim, read as lines. Below them: one column of running text with two paragraphs. No margin notes, no footnotes.

main_text.p: F L A. Vale. Anastasius, Constantinopoli post Zenonem, Ariadnæ opera, imperat, anno mundi 4454. à Christo nato 492. Hic à Græcis cognominatus est Dicoros, à discoloribus oculorum pupillis, quarū dextra nigricās, sinistra cœrulea fuit. inter bonos principes referedus veniret, quanquam humili loco ad imperiū sit euectus, nisi postea mutatus Eutychianæ hæ-resi adhæsisset: vnde illi aduersus orthodoxos graue dissidium conflatum. Legatos Indorum cum muneribus venientes, placi-dissimè audiuit. à mari ad Selymbriā longum murum duxit, ne incursiones Mysorum, Bulgarorū, & Scytharū obesse possent. Athenodorus Tyrānus in Cilicia pœnas luit: & Longinus tan-quam fera dilaniatus est. Hunni, non cōtenti Armenorum spo-liis, Cappadociā vastauerunt, & vsque ad Lycaoniam vrbes di-ripuerunt. Ad Aquilonem Vitalianus rebellauit: vt quiesceret nongēta pondo auri ab Imperatore accepit. Getæ Macedoniā, Thessaliam, Epirum diripuerunt: quibus, pro captiuis redimen-dis aurum cùm misset Anastasius, nec sufficeret hostiū votis, Barbari captiuos aut in domibus suffocarūt, aut pro mœnibus in cōspectu multitudinis trucidarunt. obiit octuagenario ma-ior, subita morte, vel fulmine tactus, ob herefim vt aiunt, impe-rij anno 28. Pom. Læ. Egna. lib. 2.

IVSTINVS Thrax, dolo imperiū adeptus est: nam mortuo Anastasio, accepta ab Amantio eunucho pecunia vt militi pro Theocritiano eligendo distribueret, in se cautè Thrax suffragia vertit. fuit primùm suùm custos, deinde boum, post lignarij cuiusdā minister, postea miles, deinde princeps ordinis, hinc Comes, dein Imperator: annis 9. optimè præfuit, & feliciter. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: Two coin medallions at the head of the page: the left shows a crowned emperor in profile, the right a radiate bust in profile. Their legends are transcribed above as lines. The page number is printed in old-style figures ("ioo" in the scan), read as 100. Reading of the medallion legends is from the engraving, with no [?] needed for the main words. Doubtful readings: "referedus" and "euectus" (ligatures), "herefim" (possibly hærefim). No marginal notes, catchword or signature are printed.
